one_line: A 60-second talking-head tip from a parenting guide on a purple studio backdrop, produced as part of a media outlet's quick-tips series, on how to get kids off screens without nagging by announcing when screen time ends and inviting them into real connection.

hook.visual: Observed: a woman in an orange top and pink trousers sits crosswise in a blue armchair against a flat saturated purple backdrop, already mid-sentence at 0:00 and gesturing with both hands. Top-left lockup of the series title, top-right red V1 logo. Large white-on-black caption in the lower third.
hook.on_screen_text: אז איך מוציאים אותם מהמסך? (So how do we get them off the screen?). Series lockup top-left: הטיפ המהיר להורים / עם עינת נתן (The quick tip for parents / with Einat Nathan).
hook.first_spoken_line: אז איך מוציאים אותם מהמסך? (So how do we get them off the screen?)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Inferred: it names a daily parent fight in one short question with no intro, spoken and captioned at 0:00, in a loud purple and orange colour block that stands out in a feed. The caption of the post adds the same pain point (they are always on the phone or computer).

beats.observed: Expert already talking, lower-third caption in white with black outline, series lockup and V1 logo visible from the first frame.
beats.spoken: Whisper: 'אז איך מוציאים אותם מהמסך?' (matches the on-screen caption exactly).
beats.on_screen_text: אז איך מוציאים אותם מהמסך? (So how do we get them off the screen?)

beats.observed: At 0:06 the whole clip shrinks into a black-outlined phone frame on the purple background while the caption reads about scrolling a feed, then snaps back to full frame. Captions are 3-6 words at a time. At 0:10 the caption 'זה די כבר עם המסך' is in red.
beats.spoken: Whisper (garbled between 0:02 and 0:05, on-screen captions used instead): if we make a face every time they choose to play on the computer or scroll an endless feed, all they hear from us is 'enough with the screen' or speeches about how bad it is, and all that achieves is that they learned to filter us out.
beats.on_screen_text: אם אנחנו / או לגלול בפיד אינסופי של / וכל מה שהם שומעים מאיתנו / זה די כבר עם המסך (red) / כל מה שזה משיג זה / שעכשיו הם למדו לסנן אותנו (If we / or scroll an endless feed of / and all they hear from us / enough already with the screen / all that this achieves / is that now they learned to filter us out)

beats.observed: Closer framing at 0:16 and 0:20. At 0:16 the caption 'אנחנו לא נגד מסכים' is in red with a thick outline, the key claim of the video.
beats.spoken: Whisper: we are not against screens, we are for life. What does that mean? That they are on screens. We want them to leave the screen, and we will not do it through guilt or threats.
beats.on_screen_text: אנחנו לא נגד מסכים (red) / מה זה אומר / אנחנו רוצים שהם יעזבו את המסך / ולא נעשה את זה דרך (We are not against screens / What does that mean / We want them to leave the screen / And we will not do it through)

beats.observed: Plain talking head, hands moving, captions continue in lower third.
beats.spoken: Whisper: simply let them know when we finish with the screen and what we will do when we finish; there must be a real invitation to connection, not a more tempting stimulus of shopping or a crazy outing. One phrase near 0:33 ('שוט לקשר') is unclear.
beats.on_screen_text: פשוט נודיע להם מתי מסיימים / ופה חייבת להיות הזמנה אמיתית / קניות או בילוי משוגע (Simply tell them when we finish / And here there must be a real invitation / Shopping or a crazy outing)

beats.observed: At 0:42 a closer, more animated shot. At 0:44 she clenches both fists with a scrunched face while the caption shows a single word 'יש', consistent with mimicking a kid's cheer (inferred). Back to calm at 0:46.
beats.spoken: Whisper: three sample lines to say: in half an hour we close the game and you come with me to the supermarket; I need to consult with you about something that happened at work; sounds like (a ride) with songs you choose. Then: and no, they are not supposed to say 'yay, fun mom, let's turn off the screen' (wording of the last clause is a guess by Whisper).
beats.on_screen_text: אז תגידו / המשחק ותבואי איתי לסופר / חייבת להתייעץ איתך על משהו / שקרה לי בעבודה / יש (So say / the game and come with me to the supermarket / I need to consult with you about something / that happened to me at work / Yes)

beats.observed: Softer delivery, open palms at 0:50 and 0:54, small smile at 0:52.
beats.spoken: Whisper: they are supposed to be frustrated when we come to pull them away, and we are supposed to prove that people are fun, that they are interesting, that they are meaningful, that we cannot do without them.
beats.on_screen_text: הם אמורים להיות מתוסכלים כשנבוא / ואנחנו אמורים להוכיח / שהם משמעותיים / שאנחנו (They are supposed to be frustrated when we come / And we are supposed to prove / That they are meaningful / That we)

beats.observed: Hands clasped. The thesis caption returns in red and bold at 0:58, the same style as at 0:16. No CTA, end card or logo animation seen in the sampled frames.
beats.spoken: Whisper: we are really not against screens, but for life.
beats.on_screen_text: אנחנו ממש לא נגד מסכים (red) (We are really not against screens)

payoff: The core tip (announce when screen time ends and pair it with a real invitation to connect, not a bigger reward) arrives at about 0:23 to 0:33, with three copyable parent lines at 0:34 to 0:44. The thesis line 'we are not against screens, we are for life' lands first at 0:16 and again at 0:58.
cta: none seen in the sampled frames or the transcript. The post caption only frames the series and the topic.
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: parents of screen-heavy kids can send it to a partner who nags, and the sample sentences ('come with me to the supermarket', 'I need your advice on something from work') are easy to save and reuse. Only 30 comments suggests it was not a debate post.
why_it_worked: Opens on the exact problem as a question at 0:00 and reframes it in the first 17 seconds with a red 'we are not against screens' line, a contrarian-but-soft angle (observed captions at 0:00 and 0:16, inferred effect).

Gives word-for-word scripts at 0:34 to 0:44 instead of general advice, which fits a like rate of 1.92% (1,470 likes on 76,546 views) while comments stay at 30 (inferred: saved or shared more than discussed).

Modest lift only: 76,546 views is 1.5x the 50,971 account median, so the format works but is not a breakout. The media brand's reach and a recurring series lockup likely did part of the work (inferred, no follower or promotion data).
paid_signal: no: like rate 1.92% is well above the 0.3% paid-promotion flag and the outlier is only 1.5x; no sponsored label visible.

solo_route.how: 1) Line up a barter expert (child psychologist, parenting guide, early-years educator) and shoot each tip as one 45 to 60 second take on a phone on a tripod against one flat saturated colour (paper backdrop or a solid wall), eye-level, expert seated. 2) Script each episode as: one-line problem question at 0:00, what does not work, one reframe sentence, 2 or 3 word-for-word parent lines, the reframe repeated as the last line; send it to the expert to edit. 3) In CapCut use Hebrew auto-captions, 3 to 6 words at a time in the lower third, put the thesis line in red, add a slight punch-in every 10 to 15 seconds, and drop the clip into a phone-shaped frame (Canva mockup) at the moment the expert mentions a feed or phone. 4) Add a series lockup top-left made in Canva and the LumeBook logo top-right, and number the episodes.
solo_route.needs: A barter expert who agrees to appear on camera and approves the final wording and captions (written consent to post). No kids needed.

lumebook_version.hook_he: הילד לא עוזב את המסך? אל תגידו 'די'. תנו לו סיבה לבוא אליכם
lumebook_version.concept: A barter parenting expert in a 'quick tip for parents' LumeBook series: end screen time with a real invitation to connect. The expert gives three scripts, one of which is 'come read a story with me'. LumeBook appears only as a logo and a 3-second end tag, no hard sell.

evidence_notes: Observed: all five contact sheets and the 0:00 and 0:06 frames, including the series lockup, V1 logo and red-highlighted caption lines. Frames are sampled every 2 s, so burned-in captions were seen only in fragments and the jump-cut or punch-in pattern is inferred from changing framing at 0:16, 0:20 and 0:42. Spoken: whisper.srt is Hebrew and reasonably good, but garbled at 0:01.8 to 0:05 ('נגמים פרצוף', 'בפידן סופי של סרטונים קולנים') where the on-screen captions were used instead, and 'שוט לקשר' at 0:33 and 'בוא תמיד את המסך' at 0:45 are unclear, so those are not quoted as exact. No music or sound effects are marked in the transcript, so none are described. Made_by: meta lists post_owner_name 'V1' and account 'einatnathan'; the V1 logo and series lockup are burned into every frame and the caption refers to the expert in the third person, and the task note says it was posted by the media outlet v1.israel, so it is classified as brand_inhouse (outlet's own series) with the expert on camera; it is unclear whether the 50,971 median in meta belongs to the outlet's account or the expert's. The woman on camera is named only as the caption and lockup state (Einat Nathan, parenting guide).
